text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card (14.5%, 613, 8.5%, 2.65, 1.87, 1%, 0 records) and the language is cautious, with an honest 'inconclusive' call and the missing documentation flagged. But the summary is generic and thin. The headline says 'too few returned records' when none came back. It cites only the single low-complexity claim and omits the 1.71 ratio, the ~37 excess 99215 claims, and the high-complexity pattern (5+ conditions at 30.3% vs 21.8% overall) that would give the 99215 excess context. Next steps are vague: no sample size, no named claims to request records for, and nothing on the 10 high-complexity 99215 claims. The investigator would have to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Headline says 'too few returned records' though zero records came back; misleading framing","Cites only one claim (C0006540), which is a single low-complexity example and does not support the broader excess-99215 point","Omits the ratio to expected (1.71) and excess 99215 claims (~37), the most direct billed-vs-expected numbers","Does not use the by-complexity table (e.g., 5+ conditions at 30.3% vs 21.8% overall; 2-condition 9.5% vs 5.2%), which would show where excess 99215s sit","Next steps are generic: no sample size, no specific claim IDs to request records for","Does not state the 1% figure as one claim of the provider's 99215 claims, which weakens its interpretability"]}
